Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When implementing a money computation, inspect ledgerly/money.py and existing helpers (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) first and reuse round_money/to_money/ZERO rather than raw arithmetic or built-in rounding.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Returning an unrounded Decimal division for a money value is a review failure; wrap the final result in round_money, and guard division by zero (empty invoice) by returning ZERO.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, all monetary values must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.content: Before implementing a new function in ledgerly, grep for existing call sites and read sibling functions (e.g. issue_invoice) to mirror their validation style: raise BillingError(code, detail) with codes like 'invalid_state', and reuse the same status-check pattern.
When validating an integer quantity, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(quantity, bool)) since bool is a subclass of int; otherwise True/False would pass a positive-integer check.

In ledgerly, Invoice.status is a plain string ('draft'|'issued'|'paid'|'void') and LineItem is a dataclass with description, quantity, unit_price; mutations should append to invoice.lines and return the created LineItem.
